# Behavioral Specification: CSRNG Environment Package

## 1. Purpose

This unit is a SystemVerilog package that supplies the complete compile-time definition of the CSRNG verification environment. It is not a synthesizable hardware block and does not implement cryptographic or random-number generation behavior. Instead, it provides the configuration constants, shared types, and environment component definitions needed to build and execute a UVM-based testbench for the CSRNG IP.

## 2. General Behavior

The package must:

- Provide a single importable namespace for the CSRNG verification environment.
- Make available all external definitions needed by the environment, including UVM base classes, bus protocol agents, push/pull agents, CSRNG agents, register abstraction models, and common DV utilities.
- Introduce UVM and DV macro definitions so that environment classes can use standard factory, message, and utility macros.
- Define no runtime hardware behavior. It shall only affect compilation and elaboration of the testbench.

## 3. Compile-Time Dependencies

The package shall be compiled only after the following categories of definitions are available:

- The UVM library.
- The project’s top-level package, including bus data-width definitions.
- Common DV utility and library packages.
- Push/pull agent package.
- CSRNG agent package.
- TileLink agent package.
- CIP base environment package.
- CSR utility package.
- CSRNG register abstraction package.

If any required dependency is missing or not compiled before this package, compilation of the package shall fail.

## 4. Configuration Values

The package shall define the following environment-wide configuration values:

- Exactly one hardware application interface shall be represented.
- Exactly one alert shall be defined, named `fatal_alert`.
- The key size shall be 256 bits.
- The block size shall be 128 bits.
- The counter size shall be 32 bits.

These values shall be fixed at compile time and shall not be changeable during simulation. The environment must use these values as the basis for interface configuration, alert checking, and cryptographic-width assumptions.

The package shall also define a 128-bit zero-seed generation pattern. This pattern shall be all zeros except for the least-significant 32-bit word, which shall have the value `0x00000004`. This pattern is intended to be used when generating a known, fully deterministic seed value for a non-FIPS-compliant instantiation.

## 5. Interrupt Classification

The package shall define an enumerated interrupt type with exactly four values. The numeric encoding and associated behavioral meaning shall be:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Command request done |
| 1 | Entropy request |
| 2 | Hardware instance exception |
| 3 | FIFO error |

The environment must use this enumeration when interpreting interrupt status, enabling coverage collection on interrupts, and checking expected interrupt behavior.

## 6. Environment Component Definitions

The package shall make available the components required to assemble a complete CSRNG UVM environment. These include:

- A configuration object that holds environment-wide settings and controls.
- A functional coverage model that records coverage-relevant CSRNG behavior and events.
- A virtual sequencer that provides a common sequencing interface for stimulus.
- A scoreboard that performs end-to-end checking of expected and observed transactions.
- A top-level environment class that assembles and connects the verification components.
- A list of virtual sequences that define reusable stimulus scenarios.

These definitions must be available when the package is imported by a UVM test. A testbench that uses this package shall be able to create and run the CSRNG environment without requiring additional environment-specific definitions outside the package.

## 7. Operational Conditions

The package must behave as follows under different usage conditions:

- **Normal testbench import:** A test that imports the package shall have access to all constants, types, and environment classes defined by the package.
- **Environment construction:** When the environment is constructed, it shall reflect the configured values: one hardware application interface, one alert, and the specified cryptographic widths.
- **Interrupt handling:** Whenever an interrupt event is observed, the environment shall interpret it according to the defined enumeration.
- **Alert checking:** The environment shall expect exactly one alert source, named `fatal_alert`.
- **Deterministic seed generation:** When a sequence needs to create a fully deterministic instantiation, it shall use the defined zero-seed generation pattern.

## 8. Constraints

This package is not parameterized. It shall represent one specific CSRNG configuration. If the CSRNG DUT is instantiated with a different number of hardware application interfaces or different alert definitions, this environment package may not be appropriate, and the mismatch must be resolved before simulation.

# CSRNG CTR_DRBG Command Handler Specification

## 1. Overview

This module handles commands for the CTR_DRBG state machine. It accepts command requests, prepares the seed/associated data needed for a CTR_DRBG update operation, obtains the updated key and V state, and produces the final command response together with the resulting working-state values.

The module supports the following command types:

- Instantiate
- Reseed
- Generate
- Update
- Uninstantiate

This module does not generate random bits. It only processes command state transitions and acknowledgments.

## 2. Command Acceptance and Ordering

- The module shall accept a command only while it is enabled.
- An accepted command shall include the command type, instance identifier, entropy value, entropy compliance indicator, additional data, current key, current V, current reseed counter, and command FIPS flag.
- The module shall provide a command-ready indication when it has space to receive a new command.
- A command shall be considered accepted only when a command request is present and the module signals that it can accept the request.
- Accepted commands shall be processed in the order in which they are received.
- While disabled, the module shall not accept new commands and shall discard any pending command data.

## 3. Command-Specific Update Preparation

For each accepted command, the module shall prepare the data to be used by the next CTR_DRBG update operation and determine the starting key, V, and reseed counter values.

| Command | Provided data for update | Starting key | Starting V | Reseed counter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Instantiate | entropy XOR additional data | all zeros | all zeros | 1 |
| Reseed | entropy XOR additional data | current key | current V | 1 |
| Generate, non-zero additional data | additional data | current key | current V | current value |
| Generate, zero additional data | no update performed | not applicable | not applicable | current value |
| Update | additional data | current key | current V | current value |
| Uninstantiate | all zeros | all zeros | all zeros | 0 |

For instantiate and reseed, if either the entropy value or the additional data is zero, the XOR result is simply the non-zero operand.

## 4. Update Execution

- For every command except a generate command with all-zero additional data, the module shall request an update operation using the prepared values above.
- The module shall wait until the update operation reports completion before producing the final command response.
- A generate command with all-zero additional data shall bypass the update operation. In that case, the module shall report the current key and V unchanged, without waiting for an update result.

## 5. Final Response Behavior

When a command has completed processing, the module shall make the result available on its final response interface. The response shall include:

- command type
- instance identifier
- key
- V
- reseed counter
- FIPS flag
- additional data

The final response shall be held until the receiving interface accepts it. A completion acknowledgment shall be asserted when the response is transferred. A status flag shall accompany the acknowledgment.

### 5.1 Response Values by Command

- **Instantiate**  
  Returns the key and V produced by the update operation, reseed counter set to 1, the original additional data, and the entropy source FIPS flag.

- **Reseed**  
  Returns the key and V produced by the update operation, reseed counter set to 1, the original additional data, and the command FIPS flag.

- **Generate, non-zero additional data**  
  Returns the key and V produced by the update operation, the current reseed counter, the original additional data, and the command FIPS flag.

- **Generate, zero additional data**  
  Returns the current key and V unchanged, the current reseed counter, zero additional data, and the command FIPS flag.

- **Update**  
  Returns the key and V produced by the update operation, the current reseed counter, the original additional data, and the command FIPS flag.

- **Uninstantiate**  
  Returns all zero state fields: zero key, zero V, zero reseed counter, zero FIPS flag, and zero additional data. The command type and instance identifier identify the uninstantiate request being acknowledged.

## 6. FIPS Flag Handling

The FIPS flag reported in the final response shall be selected as follows:

| Command | Final FIPS flag |
|---|---|
| Instantiate | FIPS flag supplied with the entropy value |
| Reseed | FIPS flag supplied with the command |
| Generate | FIPS flag supplied with the command |
| Update | FIPS flag supplied with the command |
| Uninstantiate | 0 |

## 7. Uninstantiate Behavior

For uninstantiate, the module shall carry out the required update operation using zero data, zero key, zero V, and zero reseed counter, and then respond with all working-state fields cleared.

## 8. Error Reporting

The module shall provide error indication for its internal command storage resources. Each error group shall report:

1. an attempt to store a new item when the corresponding storage is already full;
2. an attempt to remove an item when the corresponding storage is empty;
3. an invalid condition where a storage resource reports full while containing no valid item.

These error indications are intended to remain deasserted during normal operation. They may be asserted only when an internal protocol violation occurs.

## 9. Reset and Disable Behavior

- On reset, no command shall be pending, no final response shall be presented, and the module shall be idle.
- When disabled, all pending command data shall be cleared and the module shall not produce any final acknowledgment.
- After being enabled, the module shall be ready to accept new command requests.

# Behavioral Specification: CTR_DRBG Generate Completion Module

## 1. Purpose

This module completes a CTR_DRBG generate operation. It receives a generate context consisting of the current DRBG key, V value, reseed counter, compliance flag, additional data, instance identifier, and command tag. It performs one 128-bit block encryption to produce generated bits, invokes the DRBG state update operation, and returns both the generated bits and the updated DRBG state.

The module is only intended to process generate requests. A normal generate completion produces one 128-bit output block.

## 2. General Behavior

### 2.1 Reset and Disable

- When the module is reset or disabled, all internal buffered state, counters, and staged data shall be cleared.
- While disabled, the module shall not accept new generate requests and shall not produce completion acknowledgements.
- When re-enabled, the module shall return to its idle state and be ready to accept requests.

### 2.2 Request Intake

- The module shall accept a request only when:
  - the module is enabled,
  - a request is present,
  - the module has space to store the request.
- A request shall contain the full generate context:
  - command tag,
  - instance identifier,
  - compliance flag,
  - additional data,
  - current key,
  - current V,
  - current reseed counter.
- The module shall provide a ready indication that is deasserted when its request storage is full. A request that is not accepted shall be held by the requester.
- The request command tag shall be interpreted internally as a generate-block operation for the encryption phase. If a non-generate command tag is supplied, the module shall not treat it as a valid generate completion.

## 3. Generate Processing

### 3.1 Block Encryption Phase

For each accepted generate request, the module shall:

1. Form the encryption V value by incrementing the low-order counter portion of the incoming V.
   - For the configured 32-bit counter and 128-bit block, only the low 32 bits are incremented; the upper 96 bits remain unchanged.
2. Issue exactly one block-encryption request using:
   - the supplied key,
   - the incremented V,
   - the instance identifier,
   - the generate-block command tag.
3. Hold the block-encryption request until it is accepted.
4. Wait for the block-encryption completion.
5. Retain the encrypted block as the generated bits for the final result.

The module shall perform exactly one block-encryption operation per accepted request. It shall not produce multiple generated blocks within a single request.

### 3.2 Backpressure During Encryption

- The module shall not accept a new request if doing so would cause a loss of an earlier request.
- If the block-encryption service cannot accept the request, the module shall keep the request active until acceptance occurs.
- The block-encryption completion shall be stored only when there is room to receive it. If the completion storage is full, the module shall deassert its ready indication to the block-encryption service.

## 4. State Update Phase

After the generated bits have been received, the module shall perform the DRBG state update.

### 4.1 Update Request

The module shall issue an update request containing:

- the key used in the encryption phase,
- the V value used in the encryption phase,
- the additional data supplied with the original request,
- the instance identifier,
- the generate-update command tag.

The update request shall be held until the update service indicates that it can accept the request.

### 4.2 Update Completion

When the update service returns the updated key and V, the module shall combine them with:

- the generated bits from the block-encryption phase,
- the compliance flag from the original request,
- the reseed counter incremented by one,
- the instance identifier and command tag returned by the update service.

The reseed counter output shall be exactly one greater than the reseed counter value supplied with the input request.

## 5. Final Result and Completion

The final result for a completed generate request shall contain:

- 128 generated bits,
- updated key,
- updated V,
- updated reseed counter,
- compliance flag,
- instance identifier,
- final command tag.

The module shall hold the final result until the downstream consumer accepts it. When accepted, the module shall assert a completion acknowledgement and a status indication.

- For a normal generate completion, the status shall be deasserted.
- If the final command tag is not a valid generate completion, the status shall be asserted.

The module shall not generate another completion until the previous final result has been accepted.

## 6. Halt Behavior

The module supports a halt request from external control logic.

- If a halt is requested while the module is idle, the module shall stop processing new requests and enter a halted state.
- While halted, the module shall assert the halt acknowledgement.
- Requests that arrive during a halt may be buffered, but they shall not be processed until the halt is released.
- If a halt is requested while a generate operation is already in progress, the module shall finish the current operation before honoring the halt.
- When the halt request is deasserted, the module shall return to its normal operating state and resume processing any buffered requests.

## 7. Error Reporting

### 7.1 Buffer Errors

The module shall report buffer protocol errors for each internal buffering stage. For each stage, it shall flag:

- a write attempt made when the buffer is full,
- a read attempt made when the buffer is empty,
- an inconsistent buffer state in which the buffer indicates full but empty.

These error indications shall be observable on the module’s status outputs.

### 7.2 Control Error

If the module’s control logic enters an illegal or reserved state, the module shall assert a control error indication. In this condition, the module shall stop normal processing and shall not produce additional completion acknowledgements.

## 8. Supported Operational Scope

The module supports generate requests that produce exactly one 128-bit block of output. Larger generate requests must be decomposed into multiple one-block requests by upstream logic.

The module preserves the compliance flag from request input to final output without modification.

# Behavioral Specification for `csrng_state_db`

## 1. Purpose

This module is the state container for the DRBG instances used by the CSRNG block. It stores and provides access to the current working state of each instance. It does not perform cryptographic operations, generate random bits, or communicate with entropy sources.

## 2. Working State Storage

The module shall maintain a separate working state for each supported instance slot. The number of instance slots is parameterizable.

Each instance slot shall store the following fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Key | The DRBG key value, 256 bits. |
| V | The DRBG `V` value, 128 bits. |
| Reseed counter | The current reseed counter, 32 bits. |
| Active/status bit | Indicates whether the instance is currently instantiated and usable. |
| Compliance bit | Indicates whether the instance was seeded using FIPS/CC-compliant entropy. |

All fields for a single instance shall be maintained together as one consistent working state.

## 3. Reset and Enable Behavior

- The module shall have a reset input that initializes control, status, and diagnostic readback state to their idle values.
- Reset shall not by itself clear the stored working states.
- When the module enable input is deasserted:
  - All stored instance working states shall be cleared and remain zero.
  - Read outputs shall return zero.
  - Write requests shall not modify any stored state.
  - Completion/status outputs shall not indicate that a write was processed.
  - Diagnostic readback shall be disabled and shall return zero.
- When the module enable input is asserted, the module shall operate normally.

## 4. Read Behavior

When the module is enabled, the read interface shall provide the complete working state of the instance selected by the read instance identifier.

The read outputs shall include:

- The compliance bit.
- The active/status bit.
- The key value.
- The `V` value.
- The reseed counter.

The read outputs shall present a consistent snapshot of the selected instance’s stored state.

When the module is disabled, all read outputs shall be zero.

## 5. Write Behavior

The write interface shall supply:

- An instance identifier.
- A command code.
- A key value.
- A `V` value.
- A reseed counter value.
- A compliance bit.
- A status value.

The module shall be ready to accept write requests without back-pressure. A write request shall affect stored state only when the module enable is asserted.

For an accepted write, the module shall update the addressed instance slot with the supplied key, `V`, reseed counter, and compliance bit.

The active/status bit stored in the instance shall be derived from the command code:

- Commands that instantiate, reseed, generate, or update shall set the active/status bit.
- An uninstantiate command shall clear the active/status bit.

The status value supplied with the write is not stored as part of the working state. It is used only for the completion/status output.

## 6. Completion/Status Behavior

When an enabled write request is processed, the module shall produce a completion indication. This indication shall be accompanied by:

- The status value supplied with that write request.
- The instance identifier supplied with that write request.

When no write request has been processed, or when the module is disabled, the completion/status output shall be idle and shall not indicate that a write was processed.

## 7. Diagnostic Readback

The module shall provide a diagnostic readback path that exposes the working state selected by the read interface as a sequence of 32-bit words.

Diagnostic readback shall be available only when both the module enable and the life-cycle enable are asserted. If either is deasserted, the diagnostic readback output shall be zero.

The diagnostic readback path shall include:

- A control to reset the read position to the first word.
- A control to advance the read position through subsequent words.

The diagnostic output shall return the same working-state fields as the normal read interface, zero-extended as needed to align to 32-bit word boundaries.

The diagnostic readback shall reflect the instance currently selected by the normal read interface.

## 8. Instance Identifier Validity

The module shall support valid instance identifiers within the configured number of instance slots. Operation with an identifier that does not correspond to a configured slot is outside the defined behavior and shall be avoided by the surrounding design.
